notes: States and DC. units.name: Alabama

capital_gains.exemptions_thresholds: Federal: 20% bracket above USD 613,700 taxable income (MFJ, 2026); NIIT above USD 250,000 MAGI (MFJ). State: top rate reached at the thresholds stated in the summary.

inheritance.summary: Connecticut estate tax: 12% flat on the Connecticut taxable estate above the exemption, which equals the federal basic exclusion (USD 15,000,000 for 2026); total Connecticut tax capped at USD 15 million. Combined with the federal estate tax (40% above USD 15,000,000; state death taxes are deductible federally under IRC 2058), the brackets are the combined marginal rates for an estate passing entirely to children: federal tax starts once the estate net of state tax exceeds USD 15 million (about USD 15.00 million gross). Illustrative combined tax for an unmarried decedent: 11.8% of a USD 20 million estate, 33.0% of USD 50 million. Federal portability (USD 30M combined exclusion) applied on 2026-10-15: Connecticut 12% from USD 15M, combined 47.2% once the estate net of Connecticut tax exceeds USD 30M (about USD 32.05 million gross).
inheritance.exemptions_thresholds: State exemption used: USD 15,000,000 (per estate); federal basic exclusion USD 15,000,000 per person (2026), portable between spouses (state exemptions generally are NOT portable, except as noted).
inheritance.important_exceptions: Unlimited marital deduction at both levels for a US-citizen spouse; the state tax usually becomes due at the second death. Most states' exemptions are not portable, so couples use credit-shelter trusts. Bracket list is a best-faith combination of two different tax structures (see summary); it assumes no lifetime gifts, a single decedent, no other deductions.

open_questions: Connecticut DRS pages could not be opened (404); rate, cap and gift tax taken from Tax Foundation and general knowledge.
inheritance.gift_tax: Connecticut is the only state with a gift tax: lifetime taxable gifts above the annual exclusion are taxed at 12% once cumulative gifts exceed the USD 15 million exemption (unified with the estate tax). Federal gift tax also applies.
inheritance.business_relief: Federal: no exemption, IRC 6166 deferral. State-level relief for family farms and small businesses exists in several states (e.g. Minnesota qualified small business/farm deduction, Maryland family farm) but never covers a listed portfolio.

inheritance.summary: District of Columbia estate tax: exclusion USD 4,988,400 for 2026 (indexed); D.C. Code 47-3702 table taxes the estate above the zero-bracket (exclusion) amount at the band rate reached, i.e. 11.2% up to USD 5 million, then 12%, 12.8%, 13.6%, 14.4%, 15.2% and 16% above USD 10 million. Combined with the federal estate tax (40% above USD 15,000,000; state death taxes are deductible federally under IRC 2058), the brackets are the combined marginal rates for an estate passing entirely to children: federal tax starts once the estate net of state tax exceeds USD 15 million (about USD 16.76 million gross). Illustrative combined tax for an unmarried decedent: 16.8% of a USD 20 million estate, 36.5% of USD 50 million. Federal portability (married couple, USD 30M combined exclusion) applied on 2026-10-15: the federal 40% now starts at a gross estate of about USD 34.62 million.
inheritance.exemptions_thresholds: State exemption used: USD 4,988,400 (per estate); federal basic exclusion USD 15,000,000 per person (2026), portable between spouses (state exemptions generally are NOT portable, except as noted).
inheritance.important_exceptions: Unlimited marital deduction at both levels for a US-citizen spouse; the state tax usually becomes due at the second death. Most states' exemptions are not portable, so couples use credit-shelter trusts. Bracket list is a best-faith combination of two different tax structures (see summary); it assumes no lifetime gifts, a single decedent, no other deductions.

inheritance.spouse_note: Unlimited marital deduction for a US-citizen surviving spouse at federal and state level (IRC 2056); a non-citizen spouse needs a qualified domestic trust (QDOT) to defer the tax (IRC 2056(d), 2056A), so the family pays nothing at the first death only if the spouse is a citizen or a QDOT is used.

capital_gains.summary: Combined federal + District of Columbia top rate on a large long-term gain: 34.5% (federal 20% + 3.8% NIIT + state 10.75%). Top rate 10.75% on taxable income above USD 1 million; gains and dividends are ordinary income. Top marginal state rate per Tax Foundation 2026 table.
capital_gains.exemptions_thresholds: Federal: 20% bracket above USD 613,700 taxable income (MFJ, 2026); NIIT above USD 250,000 MAGI (MFJ). State: top rate reached at the thresholds stated in the summary.

inheritance.summary: Hawaii estate tax: exclusion USD 5,490,000 (not indexed); rates 10% to 20% (Tax Foundation). The bracket schedule used (10% first USD 1M above the exclusion, rising by 1 point per USD 1M to 14%, 15.7% from USD 5M, 20% above USD 10M) follows HRS 236E-8 as understood but could not be opened. Combined with the federal estate tax (40% above USD 15,000,000; state death taxes are deductible federally under IRC 2058), the brackets are the combined marginal rates for an estate passing entirely to children: federal tax starts once the estate net of state tax exceeds USD 15 million (about USD 16.61 million gross). Illustrative combined tax for an unmarried decedent: 16.9% of a USD 20 million estate, 37.9% of USD 50 million. Federal portability (married couple, USD 30M combined exclusion) applied on 2026-10-15: the federal 40% now starts at a gross estate of about USD 35.36 million.
inheritance.exemptions_thresholds: State exemption used: USD 5,490,000 (per estate); federal basic exclusion USD 15,000,000 per person (2026), portable between spouses (state exemptions generally are NOT portable, except as noted).
inheritance.important_exceptions: Unlimited marital deduction at both levels for a US-citizen spouse; the state tax usually becomes due at the second death. Most states' exemptions are not portable, so couples use credit-shelter trusts. Bracket list is a best-faith combination of two different tax structures (see summary); it assumes no lifetime gifts, a single decedent, no other deductions.

capital_gains.summary: Combined federal + Iowa top rate on a large long-term gain: 27.6% (federal 20% + 3.8% NIIT + state 3.8%). Flat 3.8%. Top marginal state rate per Tax Foundation 2026 table.
capital_gains.exemptions_thresholds: Federal: 20% bracket above USD 613,700 taxable income (MFJ, 2026); NIIT above USD 250,000 MAGI (MFJ). State: top rate reached at the thresholds stated in the summary.
capital_gains.regional_differences: Iowa's capital gain deduction covers only certain real property and business interests held long-term, not listed securities (not verified in this pass).
capital_gains.important_exceptions: State income tax is effectively not deductible federally for a top-bracket family (SALT cap; itemized deductions limited), so state and federal rates are simply added. Most states do not give a credit for foreign taxes paid. Unrecaptured section 1250 gain on real estate is taxed federally at 25% + 3.8%.

capital_gains.rate_basis: Combined effective top rate = federal 20% (IRC 1(h)) + 3.8% NIIT (IRC 1411) + Iowa top rate on long-term gains (3.8%), assets held more than 12 months, resident individual, married filing jointly, very large gain. State and federal taxes are added with no federal deduction for state tax. Local (city/county) income taxes are excluded and described in regional_differences. Federal QSBS (could make a private business sale federally exempt) is ignored.
capital_gains.professional_trader: Federal trader status (IRC 475(f)) or short holding periods turn gains into ordinary income (federal 37% + 3.8%); states taxing gains as ordinary income apply the same state rate.
capital_gains.holding_period_rules: Federal long-term treatment after more than 12 months. Most states make no distinction; exceptions are noted in the summary.
capital_gains.foreign_assets: Residents are taxed on worldwide gains at federal and state level.

dividends.summary: Combined federal + Iowa top rate on qualified dividends: 27.6% (federal 20% + 3.8% NIIT + state 3.8%). Flat 3.8%. Top marginal state rate per Tax Foundation 2026 table.
dividends.exemptions_thresholds: Federal qualified-dividend bands as for capital gains (20% above USD 613,700 MFJ, 2026).
dividends.regional_differences: Iowa's capital gain deduction covers only certain real property and business interests held long-term, not listed securities (not verified in this pass).
dividends.important_exceptions: Non-qualified dividends (e.g. PFIC funds, non-treaty foreign companies) are federal ordinary income (37% + 3.8%). Most states do not credit foreign withholding tax, so treaty-rate WHT on foreign dividends is relieved only against the federal tax.

inheritance.gift_tax: No state gift tax; lifetime gifts escape the state estate tax (subject to any add-back noted in the summary). Federal gift tax is unified with the federal estate tax (40% after the USD 15M lifetime exclusion).

inheritance.foreign_assets: Residents (domiciliaries) are taxed on worldwide intangibles; real and tangible property located in another state or abroad is generally excluded or apportioned at state level.
inheritance.domicile_rules: State death taxes follow domicile at death (intention to remain, home, voting, driver's licence, time spent). A move must be complete before death; states audit claimed changes of domicile. Non-domiciliaries pay only on in-state real and tangible property.
inheritance.spouse_note: Unlimited marital deduction for a US-citizen surviving spouse at federal and state level (IRC 2056); a non-citizen spouse needs a qualified domestic trust (QDOT) to defer the tax (IRC 2056(d), 2056A), so the family pays nothing at the first death only if the spouse is a citizen or a QDOT is used.

inheritance.foreign_assets: Residents (domiciliaries) are taxed on worldwide intangibles; real and tangible property located in another state or abroad is generally excluded or apportioned at state level.

capital_gains.summary: Combined federal + Massachusetts top rate on a large long-term gain: 32.8% (federal 20% + 3.8% NIIT + state 9%). Long-term gains and dividends are taxed at 5%, plus the 4% surtax (Millionaires' Tax) on taxable income above the indexed threshold (USD 1,083,150 for 2025; reported as USD 1,107,750 for 2026) = 9% at the top. Short-term gains: 8.5% + 4%. Top marginal state rate per Tax Foundation 2026 table.
capital_gains.exemptions_thresholds: Federal: 20% bracket above USD 613,700 taxable income (MFJ, 2026); NIIT above USD 250,000 MAGI (MFJ). State: top rate reached at the thresholds stated in the summary.
capital_gains.important_exceptions: State income tax is effectively not deductible federally for a top-bracket family (SALT cap; itemized deductions limited), so state and federal rates are simply added. inheritance.summary: Massachusetts estate tax (M.G.L. c. 65C): taxable estates above USD 2,000,000 pay tax from the 2011(b) rate table (0.8%-16%) on the adjusted taxable estate (taxable estate minus USD 60,000) less a credit of USD 99,600 (the table tax on USD 2 million), so only the excess over USD 2 million is taxed (the former cliff was removed from 2023). Marginal rates just above USD 2 million are 7.2%, reaching 16% above USD 10.1 million. Combined with the federal estate tax (40% above USD 15,000,000; state death taxes are deductible federally under IRC 2058), the brackets are the combined marginal rates for an estate passing entirely to children: federal tax starts once the estate net of state tax exceeds USD 15 million (about USD 17.10 million gross). Illustrative combined tax for an unmarried decedent: 17.7% of a USD 20 million estate, 36.8% of USD 50 million. Federal portability (married couple, USD 30M combined exclusion) applied on 2026-10-15: the federal 40% now starts at a gross estate of about USD 34.96 million.
inheritance.exemptions_thresholds: State exemption used: USD 2,000,000 (per estate); federal basic exclusion USD 15,000,000 per person (2026), portable between spouses (state exemptions generally are NOT portable, except as noted).
inheritance.important_exceptions: Unlimited marital deduction at both levels for a US-citizen spouse; the state tax usually becomes due at the second death. Most states' exemptions are not portable, so couples use credit-shelter trusts. Bracket list is a best-faith combination of two different tax structures (see summary); it assumes no lifetime gifts, a single decedent, no other deductions.

capital_gains.rate_basis: Combined effective top rate = federal 20% (IRC 1(h)) + 3.8% NIIT (IRC 1411) + Mississippi top rate on long-term gains (4%), assets held more than 12 months, resident individual, married filing jointly, very large gain. State and federal taxes are added with no federal deduction for state tax. Local (city/county) income taxes are excluded and described in regional_differences. Federal QSBS (could make a private business sale federally exempt) is ignored.
capital_gains.professional_trader: Federal trader status (IRC 475(f)) or short holding periods turn gains into ordinary income (federal 37% + 3.8%); states taxing gains as ordinary income apply the same state rate.
capital_gains.holding_period_rules: Federal long-term treatment after more than 12 months. Most states make no distinction; exceptions are noted in the summary.
capital_gains.foreign_assets: Residents are taxed on worldwide gains at federal and state level.

dividends.summary: Combined federal + Mississippi top rate on qualified dividends: 27.8% (federal 20% + 3.8% NIIT + state 4%). 4% for 2026 (from 4.4%), scheduled to fall to 3% by 2030 subject to revenue triggers. Top marginal state rate per Tax Foundation 2026 table.
dividends.exemptions_thresholds: Federal qualified-dividend bands as for capital gains (20% above USD 613,700 MFJ, 2026).
dividends.important_exceptions: Non-qualified dividends (e.g. PFIC funds, non-treaty foreign companies) are federal ordinary income (37% + 3.8%). Most states do not credit foreign withholding tax, so treaty-rate WHT on foreign dividends is relieved only against the federal tax.

inheritance.summary: Nebraska county inheritance tax: children and other immediate relatives pay 1% on what each receives above USD 100,000 (other relatives 11%, others 15%). For three children the combined exemption is USD 300,000, used as the per-estate exemption here. Spouses are exempt. Combined with the federal estate tax (40% above USD 15,000,000; state death taxes are deductible federally under IRC 2058), the brackets are the combined marginal rates for an estate passing entirely to children: federal tax starts once the estate net of state tax exceeds USD 15 million (about USD 15.15 million gross). Illustrative combined tax for an unmarried decedent: 10.6% of a USD 20 million estate, 28.6% of USD 50 million. Federal portability (married couple, USD 30M combined exclusion) applied on 2026-10-15: the federal 40% now starts at a gross estate of about USD 30.30 million.
inheritance.exemptions_thresholds: State exemption used: USD 300,000 (total for three children); federal basic exclusion USD 15,000,000 per person (2026), portable between spouses (state exemptions generally are NOT portable, except as noted).
inheritance.important_exceptions: Unlimited marital deduction at both levels for a US-citizen spouse; the state tax usually becomes due at the second death. Most states' exemptions are not portable, so couples use credit-shelter trusts. Bracket list is a best-faith combination of two different tax structures (see summary); it assumes no lifetime gifts, a single decedent, no other deductions.

sources.title: Estate and Inheritance Taxes by State, 2026
IRS releases tax inflation adjustments for tax year 2026, including amendments from the One Big Beautiful Bill

open_questions: Neb. Rev. Stat. 77-2004 could not be opened (connection refused); the 1%/USD 100,000 rule for immediate relatives is from prior knowledge, Tax Foundation shows the USD 100,000 maximum exemption and 0%-15% rates.
inheritance.gift_tax: No state gift tax; lifetime gifts escape the state inheritance tax (subject to any add-back noted in the summary). Federal gift tax is unified with the federal estate tax (40% after the USD 15M lifetime exclusion).
inheritance.business_relief: Federal: no exemption, IRC 6166 deferral. State-level relief for family farms and small businesses exists in several states (e.g. Minnesota qualified small business/farm deduction, Maryland family farm) but never covers a listed portfolio.
inheritance.foreign_assets: Residents (domiciliaries) are taxed on worldwide intangibles; real and tangible property located in another state or abroad is generally excluded or apportioned at state level.
inheritance.domicile_rules: State death taxes follow domicile at death (intention to remain, home, voting, driver's licence, time spent). A move must be complete before death; states audit claimed changes of domicile. Non-domiciliaries pay only on in-state real and tangible property.
inheritance.spouse_note: Spouses pay no Nebraska county inheritance tax (Neb. Rev. Stat. 77-2004); the federal marital deduction still applies only for a US-citizen spouse, otherwise a QDOT is needed (IRC 2056(d), 2056A).

inheritance.summary: Nebraska county inheritance tax: children and other immediate relatives pay 1% on what each receives above USD 100,000 (other relatives 11%, others 15%). For three children the combined exemption is USD 300,000, used as the per-estate exemption here. Spouses are exempt. Combined with the federal estate tax (40% above USD 15,000,000; state death taxes are deductible federally under IRC 2058), the brackets are the combined marginal rates for an estate passing entirely to children: federal tax starts once the estate net of state tax exceeds USD 15 million (about USD 15.15 million gross). Illustrative combined tax for an unmarried decedent: 10.6% of a USD 20 million estate, 28.6% of USD 50 million. Federal portability (married couple, USD 30M combined exclusion) applied on 2026-10-15: the federal 40% now starts at a gross estate of about USD 30.30 million.
inheritance.exemptions_thresholds: State exemption used: USD 300,000 (total for three children); federal basic exclusion USD 15,000,000 per person (2026), portable between spouses (state exemptions generally are NOT portable, except as noted).
inheritance.important_exceptions: Unlimited marital deduction at both levels for a US-citizen spouse; the state tax usually becomes due at the second death. Most states' exemptions are not portable, so couples use credit-shelter trusts. Bracket list is a best-faith combination of two different tax structures (see summary); it assumes no lifetime gifts, a single decedent, no other deductions.

open_questions: Neb. Rev. Stat. 77-2004 could not be opened (connection refused); the 1%/USD 100,000 rule for immediate relatives is from prior knowledge, Tax Foundation shows the USD 100,000 maximum exemption and 0%-15% rates.

inheritance.summary: New York estate tax: basic exclusion USD 7,350,000 for 2026 deaths, rates 3.06%-16% (Tax Law 952). Cliff: the credit phases out between 100% and 105% of the exclusion, so an estate above USD 7,717,500 is taxed on its WHOLE value from the first dollar. The JSON therefore uses exemption 0 and the full rate table, which is exact for taxable estates above USD 7,717,500; estates up to USD 7.35 million pay nothing. Gifts made within three years of death are added back. Combined with the federal estate tax (40% above USD 15,000,000; state death taxes are deductible federally under IRC 2058), the brackets are the combined marginal rates for an estate passing entirely to children: federal tax starts once the estate net of state tax exceeds USD 15 million (about USD 17.22 million gross). Illustrative combined tax for an unmarried decedent: 18.0% of a USD 20 million estate, 37.0% of USD 50 million. Federal portability (married couple, USD 30M combined exclusion) applied on 2026-10-15: the federal 40% now starts at a gross estate of about USD 35.08 million.
inheritance.exemptions_thresholds: State exemption used: USD 0 (per estate); federal basic exclusion USD 15,000,000 per person (2026), portable between spouses (state exemptions generally are NOT portable, except as noted).
inheritance.important_exceptions: Unlimited marital deduction at both levels for a US-citizen spouse; the state tax usually becomes due at the second death. Most states' exemptions are not portable, so couples use credit-shelter trusts. Bracket list is a best-faith combination of two different tax structures (see summary); it assumes no lifetime gifts, a single decedent, no other deductions.

inheritance.gift_tax: No state gift tax; lifetime gifts escape the state estate tax (subject to any add-back noted in the summary). Federal gift tax is unified with the federal estate tax (40% after the USD 15M lifetime exclusion).
inheritance.business_relief: Federal: no exemption, IRC 6166 deferral. State-level relief for family farms and small businesses exists in several states (e.g. Minnesota qualified small business/farm deduction, Maryland family farm) but never covers a listed portfolio.
inheritance.foreign_assets: Residents (domiciliaries) are taxed on worldwide intangibles; real and tangible property located in another state or abroad is generally excluded or apportioned at state level.
inheritance.domicile_rules: State death taxes follow domicile at death (intention to remain, home, voting, driver's licence, time spent). A move must be complete before death; states audit claimed changes of domicile. Non-domiciliaries pay only on in-state real and tangible property.
inheritance.spouse_note: Unlimited marital deduction for the surviving spouse at federal and state level (IRC 2056); the federal deduction requires a US-citizen spouse or a QDOT (IRC 2056(d), 2056A), although New York does not itself require a QDOT for its state deduction.

capital_gains.exemptions_thresholds: Federal: 20% bracket above USD 613,700 taxable income (MFJ, 2026); NIIT above USD 250,000 MAGI (MFJ). Washington: standard deduction USD 278,000 (2025, indexed) per individual or couple; 7%/9.9% split at USD 1 million of taxable gains (not indexed).
capital_gains.important_exceptions: State income tax is effectively not deductible federally for a top-bracket family (SALT cap; itemized deductions limited), so state and federal rates are simply added. Most states do not give a credit for foreign taxes paid. Unrecaptured section 1250 gain on real estate is taxed federally at 25% + 3.8%. Real estate is excluded from Washington's capital gains tax, so real estate gains bear federal tax only.

inheritance.summary: Washington estate tax for deaths on or after 1 July 2026 (ESB 6347, signed March 2026): USD 3,000,000 exclusion; rates on the Washington taxable estate after the exclusion of 10% (first USD 1M), 14%, 15%, 16%, 18% (USD 4-6M), 19%, 19.5% and 20% above USD 9 million. Deaths from 1 July 2025 to 30 June 2026 were under the 2025 schedule (up to 35%, exclusion USD 3,076,000 for early 2026). Combined with the federal estate tax (40% above USD 15,000,000; state death taxes are deductible federally under IRC 2058), the brackets are the combined marginal rates for an estate passing entirely to children: federal tax starts once the estate net of state tax exceeds USD 15 million (about USD 17.61 million gross). Illustrative combined tax for an unmarried decedent: 19.3% of a USD 20 million estate, 38.9% of USD 50 million. Federal portability (married couple, USD 30M combined exclusion) applied on 2026-10-15: the federal 40% now starts at a gross estate of about USD 36.36 million.
inheritance.exemptions_thresholds: State exemption used: USD 3,000,000 (per estate); federal basic exclusion USD 15,000,000 per person (2026), portable between spouses (state exemptions generally are NOT portable, except as noted).
inheritance.important_exceptions: Unlimited marital deduction at both levels for a US-citizen spouse; the state tax usually becomes due at the second death. Most states' exemptions are not portable, so couples use credit-shelter trusts. Bracket list is a best-faith combination of two different tax structures (see summary); it assumes no lifetime gifts, a single decedent, no other deductions.

open_questions: The exclusion is to be adjusted annually by Seattle CPI per the House amendment, while other summaries describe it as frozen; check the 2027 amount.
inheritance.gift_tax: No state gift tax; lifetime gifts escape the state estate tax (subject to any add-back noted in the summary). Federal gift tax is unified with the federal estate tax (40% after the USD 15M lifetime exclusion).
inheritance.business_relief: Federal: no exemption, IRC 6166 deferral. State-level relief for family farms and small businesses exists in several states (e.g. Minnesota qualified small business/farm deduction, Maryland family farm) but never covers a listed portfolio.
inheritance.foreign_assets: Residents (domiciliaries) are taxed on worldwide intangibles; real and tangible property located in another state or abroad is generally excluded or apportioned at state level.
inheritance.domicile_rules: State death taxes follow domicile at death (intention to remain, home, voting, driver's licence, time spent). A move must be complete before death; states audit claimed changes of domicile. Non-domiciliaries pay only on in-state real and tangible property.
inheritance.spouse_note: Unlimited marital deduction for a US-citizen surviving spouse at federal and state level (IRC 2056); a non-citizen spouse needs a qualified domestic trust (QDOT) to defer the tax (IRC 2056(d), 2056A), so the family pays nothing at the first death only if the spouse is a citizen or a QDOT is used. Washington follows the federal rule and accepts a state QDOT election.
